literal: Desire to those without, non-existent becomes sorrow; that if exists, unceasingly more and more will come.
translation: Sorrow does not exist for those who are without desire. If desire exists, sorrow will come unceasingly, more and more.
modern: ஆசை இல்லாதவர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் இல்லை. அந்த ஆசை இருக்குமானால், துன்பம் அழியாமல் மேன்மேலும் வந்து கொண்டே இருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet establishes a direct cause-and-effect relationship between desire and sorrow. For those who have completely severed desire, suffering ceases to exist. However, if even a trace of desire remains, it acts as a seed from which endless sorrows will continuously multiply and afflict them. The word 'மேன்மேல்' emphasizes the compounding and relentless nature of suffering born from desire.
